accepted_alphas.desc: Mean-reversion setup: when spread-crossing order prices look unstable (transient impact) while order-to-trade volume mean ratio indicates low conversion, expect subsequent reversal as liquidity replenishes.

Order-flow pressure proxy: when spread-crossing order price stability is high (persistent same-side aggression) and the spread-order vs trade volume mean ratio is high (weaker conversion / more submitted relative to executed), expect later mean reversion; uses long window to match the more robust persistent co-movement structure.

Interaction signal: rolling correlation between aggressive-order price stability and the SpreadOrder-to-TradeLine mean ratio distinguishes regimes where price impact is tied to poor conversion (temporary pressure) vs true execution; the sign/magnitude can be used as a regime-aware continuation/reversion predictor.
Spoof/probe signature: low stability of canceled spread-cross prices indicates rapid cancel/replace behavior; such price impact tends to be temporary and revert.

Reversion setup: lower-tail mean of price stability for spread orders; unusually unstable pricing during aggressive orders is consistent with temporary impact and subsequent mean reversion, especially when paired with low conversion in practice.

Fragility regime indicator: persistent lower-tail cancel price stability (unstable cancels) is associated with noisy/liquidity-probing flow; subsequent returns tend to mean-revert rather than continue.

Captures transient price pressure likely to mean-revert by focusing on extreme low-tail episodes of canceled spread-cross orders price stability (interpreted as instability); a persistently low-tail stability regime indicates fleeting quote moves driven by unfilled/canceled aggressors.

Delayed mean-reversion proxy: increases when canceled-order price stability exhibits downside-tail behavior (instability spikes), consistent with temporary dislocations that revert as liquidity replenishes.

Coupling between price stability of aggressive orders and conversion stress: when aggressive price stability co-moves with low fill efficiency, it suggests quote-driven impact rather than executed impact, increasing later reversal odds.

Measures whether stable (persistent) spread-crossing price action coincides with high aggressive-to-trade mean-volume ratio (fill-efficiency proxy). Strong co-movement suggests continuation; weak co-movement suggests transient pressure.

Continuation when spread-crossing flow looks like a persistent meta-order: align aggressive price stability with high order-to-trade mean-volume ratio; higher co-movement suggests sustained liquidity-taking translating into prints.

Quote-jump/mean-reversion proxy: when price stability deteriorates (more noisy quote moves) and conversion is low, moves are more likely transient microstructure noise; use rolling correlation to detect this regime.

Detects transient, cancellation-heavy quote pressure: lower-tail mean of canceled spread-crossing price stability indicates fleeting price levels likely to revert once cancellations/fragmentation dissipate.

Reversion regime: extreme low cancellation price stability (highly unstable canceled order prices) often reflects microstructure noise; lower-tail mean targets the most fragile episodes for subsequent normalization.

Robust reversion-oriented tail feature: persistent episodes of unusually low canceled-order price stability (chaotic cancel-side quoting) can signal transient liquidity shocks that revert after replenishment.
Mean-reversion setup: extreme cancel-side price instability often reflects transient quote pressure and rapid liquidity replenishment; lower-tail conditional mean to focus on extreme episodes.

Captures fragile price formation during aggressive spread-crossing: lower-tail mean of SpreadOrder price stability flags unstable price levels consistent with temporary impact and subsequent normalization.

Transient impact: low stability in spread-order prices (rapidly changing aggressor prices) often reflects fleeting pressure; episodes with unusually low stability are expected to mean-revert after several bars.
Lower-tail price stability in spread orders flags disorderly/temporary price pressure; expected to mean-revert after liquidity replenishment.

Transient impact proxy: correlation between spread-cross price stability and order-vs-trade mean ratio. Strong co-movement implies quote/price patterns are being driven by low-conversion aggressive orders, which tends to mean-revert once pressure dissipates.

Detects regime co-movement between aggressive price stability and fill-efficiency proxy. Strong correlation can indicate that the price impact is being driven by actual executions (continuation) rather than cancellations (reversion).
Temporary pressure indicator: elevated cancellation skew in spread-cross cancels during periods of unstable canceled-order prices suggests probing/spoof-like activity and subsequent mean reversion.
Buy-side cancel-driven transience: measures extreme buy-cancel volume skew specifically when canceled-order pricing is unstable, consistent with fleeting buy pressure that later unwinds.
